ETT.tex:1396 'natural', at E_0-manifolds and E_{>0}-manifolds: the natural causality over the whole family E_{>=0} is the one over the sub-family. A causality is natural over E_{>=0} iff it is natural over {E_0} (isAtlasCausalityDEC25_iff_e0), resp. over {E_kappa}_{kappa>0} (isAtlasCausalityDEC25_iff_ealpha). So the causality generated by an X_A-atlas does not depend on whether A is read as the models the manifold uses or as all of [0, oo).

findings: ETT.tex:1339-1340: the definition asserts a theorem. 'On any E_{>=0}-manifold M there is then a unique causal structure inducing that of E_alpha in every chart' is the content of cor:massA_causalite (l.1396), stated 57 lines earlier with no reference to prop:GX_sing_espace_temps_topo. It rests on (b') and hreg at the models, which the definition does not mention. In Lean it holds at every E_{>=0}-manifold (causal_Ealpha_manifolds, existsUnique_isAtlasCausalityDEC25), with 'unique' read as in OQ-18. The paper may want a forward reference to cor:massA_causalite at l.1339.

ETT.tex:1339 'unique', at a model: unique outright, absolutely minimal or not. Any causality on E_kappa, kappa >= 0, that makes every X_A-chart an isomorphism is the model's own, because the identity is such a chart (eq_massAModelCausality_of_chartIso). At a general manifold it is unique among absolutely minimal causalities. OQ-18 records that outright uniqueness fails in the gluing-free reading of defi:causalite when no chart covers M. That was shown on R u R, not on an E_{>=0}-manifold, and no E_{>=0}-manifold counterexample is built here.

ETT.tex:1340 'I^pm(x) is always an open -- possibly empty -- subset of M': openness is a standing assumption of every causality (defi:causalite, l.243; Causality.isOpen_Iplus/Iminus), so it needs no argument at E_{>=0}-manifolds (causal_Ealpha_manifolds). 'Possibly empty' happens at BTZ points: I^-_U(p) = empty for p on E_0's axis and every open U, E0.causality being E_0's natural causality over the whole family (causal_Ealpha_e0_Iminus_eq_empty).

ETT.tex:1341 'For alpha>0 the singular line is timelike, hence locally chronal': confirmed at every E_{>=0}-manifold. If an X_A-chart into E_kappa, kappa > 0, sends x to the line, the points of M read on the line near e x are chronologically ordered in every open W containing x (causal_Ealpha_lt_singLine).

To show that a sub-family's natural causality is the family's, use the uniqueness clause of massA_singular_all. A causality natural for the sub-family is absolutely minimal, and its atlas charts and sub-family charts cover M (IsoChartsCoverDEC25), so it equals the family's: isAtlasCausalityDEC25_iff_e0, isAtlasCausalityDEC25_iff_ealpha (T-ett-e-models-bprime).

A model of the family with its own causality is a witness of every E_{>=0}-manifold theorem: hcov by the identity X_A-chart (isAEChart_refl), naturality by isAtlasCausalityDEC25_model o, and uniqueness outright by eq_of_chartIso_refl (massA_singular_model, eq_massAModelCausality_of_chartIso). Then isAtlasCausalityDEC25_model (some <pi, pi_pos>) closes it by defeq (massA_dec25_models_epi) (T-ett-e-models-bprime).
